newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks power ahead at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks power ahead at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks rallied at the close Thursday mimicking a bull run on Wall Street, dealers said.
"I think the tone is firm but tomorrow could be a key session, because investors are closing their books and may take some profits," said Mariana Fabello of Banco Roberts.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 1.9 percent to 626.64, virtually erasing last week's 4.3 percent loss.
"Today gains were driven by stocks listed abroad as ADRs, especially banks and others favored by 'triple-witching' tomorrow in New York," said Gustavo Grillo of brokers Agra.

"The Dow industrial's 2.0 percent rise and the sharp fall in the U.S. long bond yield (to 6.59 percent from 6.7 percent at the opening) sent many players running to cover short positions," said Grillo.
Fabello said the bolsa would continue to closely track the U.S. treasuries market and forecast a near-term ceiling for the 30-year bond yield of 6.7 percent.
"Today we also saw some local pension funds quietly stepping back into the market, with investments mainly in (holding company) Perez Companc and in Telefonica," the trader said.

Dealers noted carmakers Sevel and Ciadea were the only MerVal stocks to buck the trend. They blamed their falls of 2.9 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively, on Brazil's decision to offer tax and import tariff incentives to auto manufacturers who invest in the country's poor north.
The broad market index closed up 1.4 percent in the session, with winners thrashing losers 42 to five and 25 stocks closing unchanged.
Floor volume picked up to 26 million pesos from 23.3 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter deals shrank to 106.3 million pesos from 146.5 million Wednesday.
Main-tier standouts were Banco de Galicia and Banco Frances, which shot up 4.5 percent and 4.3 percent respectively on strong gains in their bond holdings.
Other top MerVal gainers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, steelmaker Acindar and foods giant Molinos, which jumped 4.0 percent, 3.8 percent and 3.7 percent, respectively.
